# Resolver consumer inventory (WF-273 / SUB-12)

**Charter:** [WF-268 — C008 Centralize wf configuration and capability resolution](https://linear.app/neurasphere/issue/WF-268).
**This issue:** [WF-273 — SUB-12 Inventory resolver consumers and define query contracts](https://linear.app/neurasphere/issue/WF-273).
**Kind:** design/inventory artifact — **no runtime code.** Not read at skill runtime.
**Generated by:** claude-opus-4-8

This is the single reviewable inventory of every wf component that today performs
its own **discovery** — config, capability-registry, provider, path, and plugin-root
resolution — by re-reading files and probing the environment. It defines each
consumer's minimum typed-query requirement and assigns **every** discovered consumer
exactly once to a migration issue or an explicit named exclusion. Everything
downstream derives from here: [WF-269](https://linear.app/neurasphere/issue/WF-269)
(snapshot schema) from §7, [WF-270](https://linear.app/neurasphere/issue/WF-270)
(typed MCP tools + `/wf:resolve`) from §8.

> **Change control.** This inventory is the reviewed baseline. A **newly discovered
> consumer** — or a new skill/agent/pack surface added later — requires an **explicit
> reviewed update to this inventory and its ownership assignment**, not silent scope
> expansion into an existing migration issue. Add the row, assign the owner, get it
> reviewed.

## 1. What the resolver replaces

The charter (WF-268) adds a **project-local resolution snapshot** under `_local/`,
plus a plugin-bundled **typed MCP query adapter**, so normal skills and isolated
subagents stop reconstructing discovery per boot. The concrete discovery mechanisms
in use today — every one of which appears in the tables below — are:

| Mechanism | Where it lives today | Cost paid per boot |
|---|---|---|
| `## Capabilities` registry read | `wf.config.js` `registryPath`, **default `_local/config.md`** | 1 file read, re-parsed each run |
| `## Plugin Roots` mapping + **install-manifest self-heal** | co-located with registry; fallback reads `~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json` | 1 read + optional self-heal read |
| per-capability `manifest.md` read | each registry row's resolved `Path` | 1 read per row touched |
| provider fragment dispatch read | `inline: <rel-path>` under the capability | 1 read per surface used (body stays in caller context) |
| `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` probe | pack init capture; agent self-boot | 1 env probe |
| `wf.config.js` `registryPath` | repo root | 1 read (default-absent → `_local/config.md`) |
| `_local/config.md` config **values** | `{task-root}`, `{verify-command}`, `{qa-rules}`, `{qa-baseline-ignore}`, `## Seed`, `## Standup`, tracker sections | 1 read |
| `_local/profiles/<cap>.profile.json` | override > shipped template | 1–2 reads |
| **direct provider resolution** (`delivery`/`tracker`/`qa-execution`) | registry → manifest → fragment, scope-filtered | 1 registry + 1 manifest + 1 fragment per surface |
| **run-scoped provider forwarding** | resolved record passed down spawn messages | resolve-once, forward |

**Key invariants preserved by the resolver (from the charter):** the snapshot carries
**metadata, normalized paths, provenance, fingerprints, validity, dependencies,
provider ownership, and profiles only — never prompt or fragment bodies.** Freshness is
fingerprint/event-driven (no TTL). Existing degradation stays intact: known-stale
paths never dispatch; local reads continue; tracker writes warn-and-continue; delivery
writes block with diagnostics. Core stays capability-agnostic.

## 2. Method & coverage

Scanned exhaustively (indexed grep + full read of each surface): **every** core skill
(`plugins/wf/skills/*`), **every** core companion agent (`plugins/wf/agents/*`),
**every** pack init skill, and **every** non-init marketplace-plugin surface across all
eight current packs — wf-git, wf-ado, wf-linear, wf-node-ts, wf-audit, wf-browser-qa,
wf-angular, **and wf-review**.

**58 components** were examined: **51 are resolver consumers** (assigned to exactly one
migration owner below); **7 are explicit exclusions** (§6). The `_contracts/*` ops docs,
`references/*`, `manifest.md` files, and `profile.template.json`/registry-fixture files
are the resolver's **inputs/targets** (the data it snapshots), not consumers — they are
not counted as components.

Per-component records give **facts required · read-vs-mutation · existing degradation
class · current discovery mechanism + approximate cost · proposed resolver op(s)**. The
proposed op's **response fields and bounded response-size constraint** are defined once,
authoritatively, in §8; each row names the op(s) it maps to. This keeps the mapping DRY
and reviewable while satisfying the per-component requirement.

## 3. Discovery-mechanism taxonomy

Codes used in the "Facts / discovery" column:

- **CFG** — reads `_local/config.md` config **values** (keys named inline, e.g. `CFG:task-root`).
- **REG** — reads the `## Capabilities` registry (iterates rows).
- **ROOT** — resolves a plugin-anchored `Path` via `## Plugin Roots` + install-manifest self-heal.
- **MAN** — reads a per-capability `manifest.md`.
- **FRAG** — reads/follows a provider or phase **fragment** (dispatch); the body stays in the consumer's own context.
- **PROV:delivery / PROV:tracker / PROV:engine / PROV:host** — direct provider resolution of that surface (implies REG+MAN+FRAG+ROOT for that one surface).
- **PROF** — reads `_local/profiles/<cap>.profile.json` (override > template).
- **CPR** — probes `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` for its **own** plugin files (self-boot; see §6 note — generally out of resolver scope).
- **FWD** — consumes / produces a run-scoped forwarded provider record.
- **PATH** — resolves task-folder / workspace paths (incl. `workspace-root-resolve`, `T<NNN>` folder scans).

Read-vs-mutation column (**R/M**) is about **resolution state** only (registry / plugin-roots /
config values / profiles) — never about product source or VCS state a skill legitimately
mutates. `R` = reads resolution state; `M` = **mutates** resolution state.

Degradation classes (existing behavior the resolver must preserve):

- **bare-core** — silent local-only fallback (plain-directory read, `T<NNN>` id, no capability term).
- **tracker-warn** — tracker write warns once, then continues local-only (reads stay silent).
- **delivery-block** — delivery write blocks loudly with two-mode diagnosis (unconfigured vs registered-but-unrecoverable).
- **engine-block** — qa-execution engine/host unconfigured → capability-agnostic stop-with-diagnostics.
- **hardstop-init** — missing `_local/config.md` → stop and direct to `/wf:init`.
- **no-op** — phase firing with zero contributors → inert, byte-identical to seamless core.
- **N/A** — no provider/discovery degradation applies.

`## Plugin Roots` row and the `## Capabilities` row, seed profiles, write config
sections). Under the resolver they call core MCP `inspect_pack`/`register_pack` (R6)
instead of hand-writing the registry. Inventoried here; **migration owned by SUB-8…11**,
not by this issue's buckets.

## 6. Explicit exclusions

Components examined that perform **no resolver-relevant discovery** — assigned **no
migration owner** by name and reason:

| Component | Reason for exclusion |
|---|---|
| `plugins/wf/agents/index.md` (`wf:index`) | Pure path operator: reads/writes only the caller-supplied absolute `<task-folder>/index.md`. Zero config/registry/provider/plugin-root discovery. (The `/wf:index` **skill** #28 is the consumer.) |
| `plugins/wf/agents/classify.md` (`wf:classify`) | Only reads its **own** rubric via `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` (self-boot). No config/registry/provider. (The `/wf:classify` **skill** #23 does the discovery.) |
| `plugins/wf-angular/agents/qa-host.md` | Thin provider-dispatch shim: reads its own skill via `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`; all resolution inherited from the `qa-host` skill (#39). |
| `plugins/wf-browser-qa/agents/qa-engine.md` | Thin provider-dispatch shim: reads its own skill via `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`; resolution inherited from the `qa-engine` skill (#48). |
| `plugins/wf-node-ts/skills/test-node/SKILL.md` (`/wf-node-ts:test-node`) | Reads no config/registry/provider; consumes only the `{task-id}` folder path under `_local/` and its own `_testkit/run.mjs`. Tracker-id-shape awareness is descriptive text, not a resolution step. |
| `plugins/wf-node-ts/capabilities/node-ts/fragments/test-authoring.md` | Pure `implement`-phase **guidance** prose; zero discovery reads; applicability judged from the change under review. |
| `plugins/wf-git/capabilities/git/fragments/delivery.ops.md` (+ `delivery.md` reference half) | The delivery **provider implementation**, contract = *consume, never derive*: every op consumes an already-resolved value; reads **no** wf config/registry state. It is a resolution **target**, not a consumer. (Contrast the tracker fragments #38/#49, which **do** read their config section and are therefore consumers.) |

> **`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` self-boot is out of resolver scope.** Every skill/agent reads
> its **own** plugin files (its SKILL.md, its rubric/fragment) via `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`;
> that is the plugin runtime handing a component its own root, **not** capability
> discovery. A component whose *only* resolver touch is its own-file self-boot is
> excluded. `phase-runner` (#9) is retained as a consumer despite self-booting because
> its resolver relevance is the **per-iteration re-payment** of the wrapped phase's full
> discovery — the exact cost the resolve-once-forward design targets.

## 7. Minimum snapshot fields (WF-269)

The fields below are the **union** of what the 51 consumers actually read. WF-269 derives
the snapshot schema from this set. Per the charter: **normalized paths, metadata,
provenance, fingerprints, validity, dependencies, provider ownership, and profiles only —
no prompt or fragment bodies.**

1. **`workspaceRoot`** — normalized absolute path (from `workspace-root-resolve`; needed by run #5, init #30, and every `{task-root}`-relative join). Plain-directory value in bare-core.
2. **`registryPath`** — resolved registry location (from `wf.config.js`; default `_local/config.md`). *Consolidation win: only `init` honors a non-default `registryPath` today; the snapshot makes it uniform for all consumers.*
3. **`coreConfig`** — the core config values map: `taskRoot`, `verifyCommand`, `qaRules`, `qaBaselineIgnore`, `seed.architectureDoc`, `seed.backlogPath`, `standupStatuses`. (`{task-root}` is read by nearly every consumer.)
4. **`capabilities[]`** — the **active** registry, in order. Per capability: `name`, `manifestPath` (normalized, post-self-heal), `kind`, `fragments[]` (`phase`, `contributionKind`, `dispatch`, `scope`), `articles[]` (`key`,`value`), `requires`, `conflicts`, `profileTemplatePath`, `provenance` (`recorded`|`self-healed`). Metadata only — **fragment bodies are never stored**; the consumer still follows `dispatch` in its own context.
5. **`providerOwnership`** — surface → owner index for `delivery`, `tracker`, `qa-execution:engine`, `qa-execution:host`: `{owner, fragmentPath, state}` where `state ∈ {ok, unconfigured, unrecoverable}` (+ `candidates[]` for `unrecoverable`, for the two-mode diagnosis). This is the run-scoped resolution record, precomputed.
6. **`pluginRoots`** — `plugin → root` (normalized, post-self-heal), with provenance.
7. **`installedPacks[]`** — from `claude plugin list --json`: `pluginId`, `version`, `scope`, `enablement`, `installPath`, and snapshot `state ∈ {active, installed/inactive, installed/disabled, registered/unrecoverable}`.
8. **`profiles`** — `capability → override-merged profile values` (angular slots; audit lens-gates). Values, not templates.
9. **`providerConfig`** — provider-scoped tracker config values carried so a provider's `resolve_config` needs no second file read: `ado {project, organization, wiPrefix}`, `linear {team, project}`. (Delivery has none — *consume-never-derive*.)
10. **`idShape`** — the active tracker's id shape, or `T<NNN>` in bare-core (for id inference / minting; needs a `{task-root}` folder scan today).
11. **`fingerprints`** — per input (registry file, each manifest, `wf.config.js`, plugin-list) for fingerprint/event-driven freshness (WF-271; no TTL).
12. **`validity` / `diagnostics`** — per capability/surface resolution status + the registered-but-unrecoverable candidate diagnosis text inputs.
13. **`constitutionInputs`** — composed `article` clauses per capability + project clauses (constitution #8). Derivable from #4 + project overrides; called out because constitution is the one full-sweep `article` consumer.
14. **`slots`** *(WF-329)* — per-slot composition provenance: for each composed `<skill>.<point>`, `winningSource`, `tier` (`local-override`|`pack-contribution`|`unfilled`), `overridePresent`, `policy`, and the ordered `contributors[]`. Derived from the active pack `slot` fragments (registry order) + the presence of a `_local/slots/<skill>.<point>.md` override. Surfaced by `resolve_inspect`; body-free. Slot-contribution bodies + overrides also join the input `fingerprints` (#11) as `slot-contribution` / `slot-override` sources, and refresh fails loudly on an orphaned override/contribution (a `skill.point` no active `## Slots` interface declares).
15. **`settingsOverrides`** *(WF-329)* — the skill slugs with a present `_local/profiles/<skill>.settings.json` override (the settings-override presence index; each such file also joins #11 as a `settings-override` source). Surfaced by `resolve_inspect`.

---

## 8. Smallest typed MCP operation set (WF-270)

WF-270 derives the typed resolver queries + `/wf:resolve` from this set. **Global
response-size constraint:** every response is **metadata / normalized paths / enums /
small maps only — never a fragment or prompt body.** The fragment **dispatch read** (the
`inline:` follow) stays in the **consuming** boot's own isolated context, so diff /
artifact / fragment bodies never transit the resolver (matches run-scoped forwarding,
which "carries no fragment body").

| Op | Purpose | Response fields (bounded) | Size bound | Replaces |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **R1 `resolve_config`** | core config + workspace + registry location | `workspaceRoot`, `registryPath`, `coreConfig{taskRoot,verifyCommand,qaRules,qaBaselineIgnore,seed{…},standupStatuses}`, `idShape` | one flat map | `_local/config.md` value reads; `wf.config.js` read; `workspace-root-resolve` |
| **R2 `resolve_registry`** | ordered active registry (metadata) | `capabilities[]` = `{name,manifestPath,kind,fragments[],articles[],requires,conflicts,profileTemplatePath,provenance}` | O(active capabilities) small rows; **no fragment bodies** | `## Capabilities` read + per-row `manifest.md` reads (the phase-firing sweep) |
| **R3 `resolve_provider(surface)`** | one surface's resolution record | `{surface, owner, fragmentPath, state∈{ok,unconfigured,unrecoverable}, candidates[]?, degradation}` | one record; **no fragment body** | direct provider resolution (delivery/tracker/qa-execution) **and** the forwarded record |
| **R4 `resolve_profile(capability)`** | override-merged profile values | one profile object (values only) | one small object | `_local/profiles/<cap>.profile.json` (override>template) reads |
| **R5 `resolve_plugin_root(plugin)`** | plugin install root, post-self-heal | `{plugin, root, provenance∈{recorded,self-healed,unrecoverable}}` | one path | `## Plugin Roots` + install-manifest self-heal (`installed_plugins.json`) |
| **R6 `inspect_pack` / `register_pack`** | init write-path | inspect: `{pluginId,installPath,manifests[],valid}`; register: `{status,capabilities[],root,selfCheck}` | one status record | init hand-writes of `## Plugin Roots` + `## Capabilities` (+ profile seed, config-section write) |

**Notes for WF-270:**

- **R3 is the workhorse** — it is exactly the run-scoped resolution record (surface,
  owner, fragment path, degraded outcome). A consumer calls it once per needed surface
  and then follows the fragment itself; the **degradation semantics stay in the response**
  (`state`/`candidates`) so bare-core / tracker-warn / delivery-block behavior is
  reproduced verbatim without the consumer re-deriving it.
- **R2 serves the phase-firing consumers** (tasks #3, verify-spec #6, qa-gen #11,
  qa-auto #13, tt #15, commit's pre-commit seam #21, constitution #8): they need the
  **ordered dispatch list**, not the bodies. The `dispatch` follow stays local.
- **Provider `resolve_config`** (ado #38, linear #49) reads its config-section values
  from R1/R3's `providerConfig` (snapshot field #9) instead of re-reading
  `_local/config.md`.
- **R6 is init-only** and is the sole **write/refresh** entry — it triggers snapshot
  invalidation (WF-271). All of R1–R5 are **read-only** queries.
- **Lifecycle ops** (`refresh`, `invalidate`, `/wf:resolve` inspection) are owned by
  WF-271/WF-270 respectively and reuse the same typed service; listed for completeness,
  not derived here.

## 9. Flagged ownership decisions

Per the acceptance criterion "any consumer outside these buckets must receive an explicit
reviewed owner" — the following are **defensible best-fit assignments that a reviewer
should confirm or redirect.** They are assigned (not left catch-all), but flagged:

1. **`branch` / `commit` / `pr` skills + their agents (#17–22) → WF-286.**
   Rationale: they are the branch→commit→pr **delivery/terminal workflow** that
   terminates a task, the same family as `tf` (finalize). **Alternative: WF-278**
   (`pr` is the canonical run-scoped-forwarding *orchestrator*; `implement` invokes
   `branch`). If the reviewer reads "orchestration" as the delivery chain rather than
   phase orchestration, move all six to WF-278. They are the single largest delivery
   consumer group; keeping them together (not split across 278/286) is the priority.

2. **`constitution` (#8) → WF-278.**
   Rationale: it is a spine element — consulted as `guidance` at `spec`, enforced as
   `finding`s at `verify` — and it does the same full-registry `article` sweep as
   `tasks`/`verify-spec`. **Alternative: WF-279** (it is auto-invoked by `init` and is
   adoption-adjacent; it is also the only non-init component that **writes** the
   `## Capabilities` table, which pairs it with the init/register write-path). If the
   reviewer weights the registry-**write** behavior over the phase-**read** behavior,
   move to WF-279 or couple it with the WF-274 register path.

3. **`tt` (#15) → WF-286 (QA).** Low-risk: `tt` is test authoring (QA-adjacent) and
   terminal-ish. **Alternative: WF-278** if "test authoring at implement" is read as a
   phase/spine concern. Noted for completeness.

No consumer was placed in a catch-all; every one of the 51 has a named owner above.

---

## 10. Documented contract-completeness gaps

Surfaced because WF-269/WF-270 must decide whether the snapshot/op set covers them or
explicitly excludes them (they are **not** silent omissions):

- **`verify-spec` (#6) / `verify-fix` (#7) evidence gathering** — diff / HEAD-SHA /
  base-SHA / dirty-tree inspection has **no delivery operation today**; it reads the
  local working tree directly regardless of provider state. If WF-270 wants this behind
  the contract, a `delivery` read op (e.g. `working-tree-state-read`) is needed;
  otherwise document it as a deliberate local-only read outside the resolver.
- **`qa-run` (#12) `Tester` identity** — resolves "the environment's configured user
  identity"; the delivery surface has **no identity/user operation**, so it never routes
  through a contract call. WF-270 should either add an identity op or document it as
  out-of-contract.

These gaps do not block the inventory; they are inputs the two downstream issues must
consciously resolve.
